steps.title: Task specific pretrained weight fine tuning

blocks.text: Adapt the supplied ViT image classifier in a bounded supervised task. Keep original pretrained and task label mappings distinct.

Import torch, nn from torch, and AutoImageProcessor, ViTForImageClassification, TrainingArguments and Trainer from transformers. Load the compatible checkpoint with ViTForImageClassification.from_pretrained(checkpoint); retain its original label mapping for the baseline. Load AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(checkpoint). Processing images with return_tensors="pt" gives pixel_values; model(**inputs).logits gives logits. Use this processor for both training and validation. With supplied preprocessed datasets and collator, configure TrainingArguments with output_dir, num_train_epochs, per_device_train_batch_size and learning_rate as declared, eval_strategy="epoch" and remove_unused_columns=False. Configure Trainer with model, args, train_dataset, eval_dataset=validation_dataset, data_collator and processing_class=processor. Trainer.train() performs the bounded adaptation.

blocks.text: For classifier-only adaptation, set existing parameters’ requires_grad=False, then replace model.classifier with nn.Linear(model.config.hidden_size, num_labels). Update model.num_labels, config.num_labels, config.id2label and config.label2id to the task mapping. New head parameters are trainable by default. Verify changed head weights and unchanged frozen backbone. Compare task predictions with the frozen pretrained reference on the same validation cohort, without an application or protected-test data. Binary FPR = FP/(FP+TN) conditions on actual negatives; FNR = FN/(FN+TP) conditions on actual positives. Empty conditioning groups give undefined rates.

items.text:
```python
import torch
from torch import nn
from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, ViTForImageClassification, TrainingArguments, Trainer
model = ViTForImageClassification.from_pretrained(checkpoint)
original_mapping = dict(model.config.id2label)
processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(checkpoint)
# Retain frozen pretrained outputs with original_mapping on validation_images.
for parameter in model.parameters(): parameter.requires_grad = False
model.classifier = nn.Linear(model.config.hidden_size, num_labels)
model.num_labels = model.config.num_labels = num_labels
model.config.id2label = id2label
model.config.label2id = label2id
args = TrainingArguments(output_dir=output_dir, num_train_epochs=epochs, per_device_train_batch_size=batch_size, learning_rate=learning_rate, eval_strategy="epoch", remove_unused_columns=False)
trainer = Trainer(model=model, args=args, train_dataset=train_dataset, eval_dataset=validation_dataset, data_collator=data_collator, processing_class=processor)
trainer.train()
```
Review evidence: checkpoint processor supplies pixel_values for train and validation images; original reference mapping remains distinct from the two-class task mapping. Snapshot comparisons show changed head values and identical frozen backbone values. The four-image shape fixture produces logits `(4, 2)` and long targets `(4,)` with indices 0 or 1. Separately, a two-image adaptation verification minibatch produces logits `(2, 2)` and long targets `(2,)`. The following X, D, loss backward pass and inspected `classifier.weight.grad.T` all belong to that two-image minibatch; D already includes that loss’s reduction. The selected loss is backpropagated after clearing old gradients. Head-gradient comparison expresses the head as Z = XW + b, where W is classifier.weight.T; the inspected gradient is classifier.weight.grad.T. It uses X.T @ D, D already contains reduction; X=[[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]], D=[[-0.1, 0.1], [0.2, -0.2]], reference=[[0.5000000000000001, -0.5000000000000001], [0.6000000000000001, -0.6000000000000001]]. Computed selected gradient agrees at declared rtol/atol. Same-cohort validation rates and costs follow the supplied table, adapted cost is lower under the stated rule; no protected-test data is accessed. An empty actual-negative group returns undefined FPR (None), not zero.
All parameters are frozen after replacing the classifier, including the new head; the review claims classifier-only supervised adaptation succeeded without checking changed head weights.
The selected head-gradient reference divides X.T @ D by the minibatch size again although D already includes the loss reduction.
The pretrained reference uses one validation cohort and the adapted head uses a different cohort; the review attributes their cost difference solely to adaptation.
Rate review for the adapted counts in the table: FPR is reported as FP/(FP+TP) = 0.1111111111111111.
Cost review replaces the supplied deployment probabilities and unequal error costs with an unweighted average of FPR and FNR, reporting adapted cost 0.15000000000000002.
A cohort has no actual negatives, and the returned report defines FPR=0 rather than marking it undefined.
Protected test images are used to tune epochs and choose the lower-cost checkpoint.

i1.message: The excerpt preserves the pretrained reference and processor, freezes only existing parameters before making a trainable task head, verifies shapes/gradient and changed head versus unchanged backbone, and compares conditional costs on matched validation with undefined-rate handling.

i2.message: The new classifier must receive supervised updates and show changed values; freezing it contradicts that criterion.

i3.message: Reduction is already in D; another division produces the wrong chain-rule reference.

i4.message: The comparison requires the same validation observations for both prediction sets.

i5.message: FPR conditions on actual negatives and uses FP+TN, not predicted-positive counts FP+TP.

i6.message: The supplied expected-cost contract weights each conditional rate by its deployment class probability and corresponding error cost; an unweighted average is not that cost.

i7.message: FP+TN is zero, so the conditional false-positive rate is undefined.

i8.message: Using protected test observations for settings or model choice leaks information into the chosen system.
